- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (positive sentiment → model tends to overshoot).
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is consistently negative or trending down.
- Model overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts, especially when sentiment turns sharply positive.
- Forecast tends to peak too early after a spike, then overcorrects downward — adjust for lagged mean reversion.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly negative, model often fails to account for downward drift — apply mild downward bias.
- Avoid overconfidence in 30-day forecasts when recent sentiment is volatile — reduce peak magnitude by 5–10%.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative swings, model should not overcorrect upward — cap upward revisions at 3–5% above recent low.
- When sentiment is positive but recent prices are falling, model should not assume continuation — apply downward bias to avoid “sentiment trap.”
